question.prompt:
Triangle \(ABC\) is inscribed in a circle with center \(O'.\) A circle with center \(O\) is inscribed in triangle \(ABC.\) \(AO\) is drawn, and extended to intersect the larger circle in \(D.\) Then we must have:

[Figure 1](figures/1966_AMC_12_Q31_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The incircle's center lies on the triangle's internal angle bisectors. This connects the line \(AD\) with both circle angles and angles involving \(O\).

[Figure 1](figures/1966_AMC_12_Q31_question_fig1.svg)

Write \(\angle BAC=2\alpha\) and \(\angle ABC=2\beta\). Since \(O\) is the incenter,
\[
\angle BAD=\angle DAC=\alpha,
\qquad \angle ABO=\angle OBC=\beta.
\]
The ray \(AO\) passes through the triangle's interior, so its second circle intersection \(D\) lies on the arc \(BC\) not containing \(A\).

Draw \(BD\), \(CD\), and \(BO\). Inscribed angles subtending the same arcs give
\[
\angle CBD=\angle CAD=\alpha,
\qquad
\angle BCD=\angle BAD=\alpha.
\]
Thus triangle \(BCD\) has equal angles at \(B\) and \(C\), so \(BD=CD\).

To compare these lengths with \(OD\), consider triangle \(BOD\). Ray \(BC\) lies between \(BO\) and \(BD\), so
\[
\angle DBO=\alpha+\beta.
\]
Meanwhile, the angle sum in triangle \(AOB\) gives
\[
\angle AOB=180^\circ-\alpha-\beta.
\]
Because \(A,O,D\) occur in that order on one line, \(OA\) and \(OD\) are opposite rays. Therefore
\[
\angle BOD=180^\circ-\angle AOB
=\alpha+\beta.
\]
Triangle \(BOD\) consequently has equal angles at \(B\) and \(O\), giving \(OD=BD\). Combining the two equalities,
\[
\boxed{CD=OD=BD},
\]
which is choice D.
solutions.title: Find two isosceles triangles
